issues.title: eval --file and eval --stdin are broken — always produce browser_evaluate error

sections.body:
echo 'document.title' > test.js
./b4w.sh eval --file test.js
Result: Error: ERROR: browser_evaluate failed: Unexpected error in [evaluateValueDetail]

Same with --stdin: echo 'document.title' | ./b4w.sh eval --stdin
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The JavaScript from the file or stdin should be evaluated in the browser context and return the result, same as inline eval.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Both --file and --stdin always fail with 'browser_evaluate failed: Unexpected error in [evaluateValueDetail]' regardless of script content, even for trivial expressions that work fine inline.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The --file and --stdin code paths likely differ from the inline eval path in how they call the backend's evaluate function. The error message references 'evaluateValueDetail' which suggests the code is wrapping the expression differently or passing an incorrect selector parameter. The SKILL.md explicitly recommends --file and --stdin for Windows users to avoid shell quoting issues — having these broken makes eval effectively unusable for complex scripts on all platforms.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: Likely in the CLI's eval command handler (cli/browser4-cli/src/) or the backend's MCPToolController.kt — the evaluateValueDetail function appears to receive a null/malformed selector when the --file/--stdin path is used.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Fix the --file and --stdin eval paths to correctly pass the JavaScript expression to the browser without requiring a selector parameter
- Add a test that verifies eval --file and --stdin work for simple expressions
- Consider unifying the code path so inline, --file, and --stdin all use the same evaluate function
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Amazon uses multiple nested elements with the same price data for different screen sizes (responsive design). The text extraction concatenates all visible text nodes including those meant to be hidden via CSS at certain breakpoints but still present in the DOM.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: Backend text extraction logic — could filter out visually hidden text nodes or deduplicate concatenated currency+value patterns.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Consider filtering out elements with display:none or visibility:hidden during text extraction
- Add a --clean or --visible-only flag to text extraction that skips hidden elements
- Implement smart deduplication for common patterns like 'TWD123TWD123'
